newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil stocks close higher amid strong trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazil stocks close higher amid strong trade.

text.p: Brazilian stocks ended higher again Tuesday as a strong influx of local fund investment and optimism about privatizations in the telecommunications and power sectors continued to bolster share prices, brokers said.

The Sao Paulo bolsa's Bovespa index of 47 leading shares end up 0.81 percent at 13,043 points on hefty volume totalling 1.152 billion reais ($1.07 billion). The market closed before the government announced the resignation for personal reasons of Central Bank President Gustavo Loyola. Bank International Affairs Director Gustavo Franco was named as his replacement.
Traders and analysts said the market was likely to react positively Wednesday to the changes at the central bank.
"It was positive not because Loyola left but because Franco will replace him. He is someone who is well known by the markets," one partner at a local bank said.

The day's trade was bolstered by a strong flow of cash from domestic funds and general optimism regarding the prospects for selling off federal telecoms holding Telebras and upcoming power sector privatizations.
The bolsa's benchmark share, Telebras preferred, ended 0.74 percent higher at 163.70 reais.
